text:
A rich man lived in a big house. Next door lived a poor shoemaker. Every morning, the shoemaker sang happily while he worked.

The rich man could not sleep because of the singing. He was angry. “Why is he so happy?” he thought. “I have more money, but I am never happy.”

One day, he called the shoemaker. “Here is a bag of gold,” he said. “It is a gift for you.”

The shoemaker was very surprised. He took the gold home. He hid it under his bed. But now he worried every day. “What if someone steals it?” he thought. He could not work well, and he stopped singing. At night, he could not sleep.

After a few days, he took the gold back to the rich man.

“Please take it back,” he said. “I want my songs and my sleep. They are worth more than gold.”

The rich man understood. He smiled for the first time in many days.

Moral: Happiness is more valuable than money.
